claim: The acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not met. When no SurrogateType is given, Collect always uses CreateContractlessMembers, which ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract] and [DataMember] on T. A T marked [MessagePackObject] with [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] therefore gets a string-keyed map formatter instead of an int-keyed array formatter, and an [IgnoreMember] property is still serialized. The maintainer's rule was 'if there is no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject] attribute on the type, go contractless', which implies those attributes switch contractless mode off.

claim: Contractless mode silently drops public get-only properties and does not honour [IgnoreDataMember] on T. claim: In the default (no SurrogateType) path, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`. That path ignores every MessagePack attribute on `T`: `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]` and `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` are never read. A `T` with `[IgnoreMember] public string Secret { get; set; }` therefore still has `Secret` serialized. Members marked `[Key(0)]` or `[Key("v")]` are written under their member names as string keys instead of the declared keys. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.' The output is also not byte-compatible with the formatter the defining assembly's own resolver produces.

claim: `needsCast` compares `m.Name` with "OnBeforeSerialize"/"OnAfterDeserialize" only for methods that have ExplicitInterfaceImplementations. An explicit implementation's Name is the qualified "MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize", so the check never matches. It also inspects only `type.GetMembers()`, not base types, and private explicit impls are not imported from metadata. As a result, any `T` that implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver explicitly gets `needsCast = false`. The template then emits `value.OnBeforeSerialize()`, which fails to compile (CS1061) in the generated code.

claim: The generated partial class is emitted with only the 'partial class' modifiers. It is emitted inside EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces and carries the generic constraints and formatter name from Info.Formatter. The analyzer never checks whether the user's declaration is a class nested in a generic or static container, or is 'sealed' or 'static'. The accessibility of the formatter, which is user-declared, does not matter for the partial. The main compatibility risk is the resolver: the generated resolver registers Info.Formatter as if it were a generated 'internal sealed' class. A user-declared public formatter may be instantiated through a different path, such as 'new Formatter()'. The user-declared formatter may also lack a parameterless constructor, which would break the generated resolver.

claim: Contractless mode serializes members sorted by ordinal name and silently drops get-only or private-set properties, readonly fields and init-only properties that would normally be serialized. Because IsPublicReadWrite requires a public setter, init-only properties are included (their SetMethod is public) while the info is marked IsInitOnly. The sort order is name-ordinal, whereas the existing contractless resolver uses declaration order. Bytes for a type serialized through this formatter therefore differ from the dynamic ContractlessStandardResolver for the same type, which breaks interoperability for users who later switch resolvers. This follows from the requirement but is not documented.

claim: Each [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] model is added to `modelPerType` unconditionally. If `T` is also a [MessagePackObject] type in the same compilation, or two generated formatters target the same `T`, two ObjectSerializationInfos for the same data type reach the resolver. Depending on the resolver template and the ObjectInfos comparer, this either drops one formatter silently (sorted-set dedupe) or registers `typeof(T)` twice in the resolver lookup, which throws at type initialization. No diagnostic is reported for the duplicate.
